chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: Finding the big building for the Black and Tan nightclub
summary: Turner told his Italian boss about a vacated furniture store on Independence and Charlotte, which became the Black and Tan.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: We used to have...we finally got a nightclub, and one of 'em had no liquor there. Back in the Prohibition days, we got a nightclub called The Cherry Blossom. No, it was The Suns... It was the Black and Tan. 'Cause we named it Black and Tan but it was a big furniture store on the corner of Independence Avenue and Charlotte.

So, somehow or other, the furniture store closed and moved out. So I told the dago boss that I know where to get him...to have a fabulous nightclub at, so he was lookin' around, say, he wanted a bigger place, so I say, I told him, I say, "I know where you get a bigger place at. Make a beautiful nightclub." There wasn't but about five or six blocks down the street but the dago ain't paid no attention to it.
Say, "Where..." He called me Daddy Long Legs. Say, "Where's it, Daddy Long Legs?"

So he got a...he had a Packard car, a big old Packard car-- even have a sireen on it...like the policemen's. So we get in the car, and we drive down there, and I showed it to him. I said, "That's the place. Right there." So, there was somebody in there, cleanin' up the place. So we went on in and looked it over. Say this would make a nice nightclub. It was what you call a real nightclub...this'd make a beautiful nightclub...was a great, big place, had a big balcony all 'round it. At the top, there's a big balcony. Down in the bottom...it was a huge place. So we say, "This is where it's at. We can put the white folks over here on one side of the balcony...and really have a nice nightclub. You know."
So we got so we finally took it over and opened it up. We call it The Black and Tan Nightclub. So the Black and Tan was on and runnin'.
